narration: Watching videos feels productive, until you try solving alone. Blitz Learning is our engineering prototype turning passive video watching into active math practice. On our neutral front door, future subjects say coming soon while math is playable now. Learners pick a math quest, a problem, and an original nonhuman tutor: a robot, fox, or fantasy creature. These real captured screens show controlled local practice, not live AI. An offline deterministic checker grades numeric answers: one to three consecutive correct fresh questions earn one to three stars, and errors reset streaks, not best stars. Next, our architecture pairs Gemini 4 Argon for explanations with Gemini Live for optional voice discussion and consented written work photos. Our roadmap adds more subjects, outcome evaluation, privacy hardening, and explicit check ins, never facial tracking.

claimsToAvoid: Claiming proven learning gains, validated test-score improvements, or a finished production service.
Implying the captured UI screen recording itself is executing live Gemini AI calls during the controlled local practice demo.
Inferring or claiming to detect facial emotion, gaze, attention, identity, age, disability, or comprehension from camera input.
Allowing Gemini explanation failures or model outputs to grade numeric answers, award stars, or override the local deterministic checker.
Proposing live humanlike avatars, human anime agents, or copyrighted franchise characters.
